title: Console visual language & component audit: unified tokens, dashboard, rollout, and cost patterns
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Audit and unify the Console visual language across dashboards, rollout management screens, and cost breakdown views. Deliver a Figma library (tokens + components) and a lightweight token export format for platform engineering. This ticket covers: token naming conventions, color/contrast decisions for cost charts, component variants for rollout states (canary / stable / failed), standardized KPI card and table patterns, and a performance-aware Figma structure to reduce file bloat. The goal is to provide a single source of truth for UX, speed future feature work, and reduce inconsistent surface-area regressions in the Console.
background: Multiple product areas shipped independently over the last two years; we now have inconsistent token names (primary vs brand vs core), duplicate button styles, and three different chart color palettes used by dashboards, rollout charts, and cost views. Engineering has asked for a compact token JSON export to embed in runtime CSS and a mapping doc for legacy tokens. Product has a near-term rollout for cost-visibility improvements and wants consistent KPI cards for the release in March.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library published with: core tokens file (colors, type, spacing), component library file (cards, buttons, tables, rollout banners), and a usage guide page
Token export (JSON + human-readable mapping) checked into platform-design-assets and consumed in a sample console page by ENG-3182
High-contrast color palette defined for charts and cost breakdowns that passes WCAG AA for normal text and WCAG AAA for small UI labels used in KPI cards
Rollout component variants built: default, canary, degraded, fallback, and paused; patterns documented with recommended fallback rules
Design sign-off from PM (Julia Kim) and Eng lead (Carlos Mendes) and at least one usability pass with Solutions Engs (notes attached)
decision_log: Token naming convention chosen: rdx-{category}-{purpose} (e.g., rdx-color-surface, rdx-space-2, rdx-type-heading-2) to avoid collisions with platform tokens
Chart palette: use four semantic color stops (rdx-color-balance-positive/neutral/negative/highlight) with enforced contrast ratios; cost bars use highlight for estimated spend anomalies
Figma structure: split into 'Core Tokens' + 'Platform Variants' files. Keep 'Console Components' as a lightweight library with instances to avoid large embed layers
Rollout UX: show canary percentage with micro-graph sparkline; fallback policy should be exposed as an affordance not a modal to reduce disruption during incidents
Accessibility: text labels on KPI cards must remain visible at small sizes; moved subtokens for microcopy to rdx-type-caption-scale to support localization
notes: Initial scan found 27 duplicate color tokens across 5 files — consolidated to 9 core color tokens and 6 platform utility tokens
Figma file size was causing slow load for engineers during reviews; resolved by splitting tokens into a separate file and converting large example pages into flattened images for reference

Trade-off: keeping a small token set improves developer ergonomics but reduces design granular control. We documented extension points so feature teams can add feature-specific tokens under 'feature/*' namespaces
Prototype A (high-contrast cost panes) favored by PMs for readability; Prototype B (brand-forward) flagged for failing contrast on small labels
